name: astrology

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Celtic interest in astrology began with the stars, which the Celts knew well because they lived outdoors much of the time. They may have turned this knowledge into an arcane science in which the changing patterns of the planets affected life on earth. Julius Caesar claimed the druids were master astrologers. In Ireland the starting date of St. Columba's education was fixed by star aspects, and legend says the druid Cathbad cast a horoscope to see the future of the child who became Deirdre of the Sorrows. Only faint hints of the system survive, including the Irish word néladóir, used of one who divines from the sky. The word also translates as "cloud-diviner." The Celts passed such powerful material orally, so no Celtic astrological text is likely to be found. Koch notes that medieval Celtic month and quarter-day names tracked the seasons and weather rather than the stars.

okr.objective: Establish the scanty evidence that the Celts practiced a form of astrology.
